This study provides a detailed examination of the potential issues with the popular practice of employing contextualized word embeddings for detecting diachronic semantic shifts in a specific corpus, the English Wikipedia. Focusing on the BiDi task, where the goal involves identifying words whose meanings have undergone a significant change within a short period, our research shows that while score distributions in this practice tend to be heavily centered around zero with long tails, many instances of words with notable semantic changes are overlooked. Our analysis delves into the limitations of contextualized embeddings and proposes a more thorough evaluation of scoring metrics that takes into account extreme values, showcasing that traditional methods of detecting diachronic semantic change are insufficient to fully assess the accuracy and reliability of this complex task.

Active galactic nuclei (AGN) containing active black holes at the center of their host galaxies can provide valuable information about the mass and spin of black holes through analyses of their electromagnetic spectra. To take full advantage of this, the electromagnetic events catalog of the Swift Gamma-ray Multi-satellite has been updated to include the Swift-Archipelagos (SAA) project, which searches for specific features in the X-ray and ultraviolet spectra resulting from the accretion of matter onto black holes. The SAA project utilizes Swift-Archipelagos to look for the iron K$\alpha$ and oxygen VII lines as well as hydrogen Ly$\alpha$ to determine the spin of supermassive black holes in AGN. When examining the SA0 events of the Swift-Archipelagos catalog, the lines were searched for in the X-ray and ultraviolet spectra, with the iron K$\alpha$ and oxygen VII lines showing a marginal detection at 2$\sigma$ significance, while the spin is consistent with previous measurements of the mass and spin of black holes in AGN.

A distinctive feature of neural development is the rhythmic shifting of cell nuclei
between the upper and lower layers of the neuroepithelial tissue as interkinetic nuclear
migration (IKNM) unfolds. In this study, we utilize extended, high-speed two-photon
imaging to track the movement of individual nuclei in the developing mouse olfactory bulb
during IKNM. From these observations, we extract the migration velocities and apply
supervised learning to identify any variations in the rate of nuclear movement. Our results
reveal that the length of a nucleus's stay in the upper layer of the neuroepithelium depends
on the stage of its development, specifically, the time it takes for the nucleus to reach
maturation increases as the olfactory bulb undergoes expansion. To better understand
this phenomenon, we relate the changes in migration velocity to the local volumetric
expansion rate derived from the changes in the curvature of a boundary between the upper
and lower layers of the neuroepithelium. Based on this relationship, we estimate the
increase in volume of the olfactory bulb during expansion and confirm that the changes in
curvature accurately reflect the actual volume changes occurring within this tissue.

In various image processing tasks, including video compressed sensing and color image demosaicing, images must be separated from coded measurements that represent their superposition. Real-world code patterns, which are often non-negative, systematically structured and non-Gaussian, can impede reconstruction due to their non-ideal coherence properties. This research addresses this challenge by developing optimized code patterns that minimize the coherence of the sensing matrix and division matrix joint sparsity model, with the goal of enhancing the sparsity of the reconstructed signal, considering possible distortions and noise, and presenting a greedy reconstruction algorithm to solve this model, and demonstrating its effectiveness through improved reconstruction performance in simulated and real-world experiments.

We've developed a comprehensive hydrodynamic theory that applies to polar active fluids in the presence of randomly distributed inclusions, and our model demonstrates the possibility of overcoming these obstructions to maintain a non-zero overall speed. Contrary to previous assumptions, the dynamics of this specific class of active matter cannot be accurately captured using simplified hydrodynamic models when the spatial environment is two-dimensional up to five-dimensional space; however, we were able to derive precise, dimension-dependent scaling parameters for these dimensions.

Researchers within the same institution often rely on their institutional email as their primary means of communication. Due to their accessibility and private data storage, these emails are vulnerable to cyber threats and can serve as lucrative targets. Our proposed vulnerability assessment approach utilizes open-source data, including the Cyber Kill Chain, to analyze research institutions' communication networks and identify potential risks. We executed our method on three American research institutions, incorporating their email traffic and discovered that examining real-world data can reveal susceptible nodes without exposing private data. Our results show that a considerable percentage of the examined nodes are at risk, indicating the necessity for integrating email security into overall security strategies. Moreover, our findings demonstrate the value of considering network structure when evaluating the vulnerability of systems, as opposed to examining isolated components in isolation.

Inspired by the pseudogap phenomenon in cuprates, we propose a new idea, 
the "exceptional" or "split-merger" van Hove singularity, useful in systems 
with strong electron interactions. This concept arises when a lattice symmetry 
breaking lowers the electron interaction strength and induces a merger of 
separated Fermi-surface pockets into a large, continuous Fermi surface, 
induced by a van-Hove singularity. A theoretical model is developed using 
Hubbard-U on a square lattice to demonstrate how this singularity can emerge, 
using orbitally-degenerate electron states as an intermediate symmetry phase, 
and electron-phonons as the mechanism for lattice symmetry breaking. We show 
that a ferromagnetic order on the square-lattice halves both the electron 
interaction, via a Bogoliubov transformation, and the lattice periodicity, 
via a unit cell doubling. This model yields a particularly interesting phase 
diagram, where the electron-phonons drive a flow towards a large, closed 
Fermi-surface, for a specific range of interaction strengths. A resistivity 
calculation also reveals that the model can produce a resistivity transition, 
distinguishing the electron-phonons in the normal state, and the purely 
magnetic phases in the ordered state.

This paper details a specialized apparatus built for use in Aberdeen Tunnel's laboratory in Hong Kong. The laboratory is uniquely situated to study spallation neutrons produced by cosmic-ray muons with 611 meters of water equivalent in depth. The apparatus consists of six layers of horizontal plastic-scintillator detectors that pinpoint the direction and location of incoming muons. Between these layers, a neutron sensor filled with 650 kilograms of liquid scintillator containing a gadolinium dopant significantly enhances detection efficiency of the produced spallation neutrons. Additionally, we discuss the performance characteristics of this apparatus.

Ground-based observations of planetary movements caused by the gravity of their host stars are crucial for confirming the validity of exoplanets discovered by the Kepler and TESS space telescopes. Although space-based detectors provide high-precision data, the ground-based telescopes offer fuller insights into the physical properties of these distant planets and their stars. However, planet confirmation processes face delays and often suffer from inefficiencies. We propose an end-to-end pipeline that streamlines planet confirmations by integrating data from the TESS and TESS Ground Based Surveys, using artificial neural networks trained with interpretability techniques to minimize human involvement. By integrating these approaches, we achieve a degree of automation and plan for optimal resource allocation at the TESS Ground Based Surveys site to maximize the efficiency of planet confirmations.

The growth of Information Technology has significantly altered how information is shared, making it necessary to convert printed documents into digital formats.  There has been an increase in fraudulent activities lately, prompting the need for quicker verification methods.  To facilitate this, a method has been devised that combines Video Rate Document Verification and Optical Character Recognition to convert ID cards from various countries into machine-readable text.  Deep Learning techniques have been employed to enhance document segmentation and character recognition, resulting in a comprehensive database of text information for ID cards from around the world.  To evaluate the accuracy of our approach, we experimented with images of ID cards from different countries, prompting the optical character recognition system to produce a machine-readable output.  Our results show a character accuracy rate of 0.97, and our method has been made available on the Google Cloud Platform.

Quantum harmonic oscillators were computationally analyzed in their ground state with either steady-state driving forces varying in intensity or driving forces that changed over time. Calculations of position expectations were carried out for multiple scenarios of mass, angular frequency, and the lambda parameter in both cases. Constant driving led to coherent states, with theoretical predictions closely matched by both simulation approaches. A discrete-time lattice Metropolis algorithm was used to evaluate the imaginary time path integral for these simulations.

The Yarkovsky-O'Keefe-Radzievskii-Paddack effect significantly influences the rotational states of small asteroids by exerting a net torque resulting from solar radiation reflected and re-emitted by the surface. As a consequence of this phenomenon, the rotation period of these asteroids gradually changes, either shortening or lengthening, depending on whether the Yorp torque accelerates or decelerates the rotation. This effect is directly tied to the orientation of the spin axis, typically represented by the inclination and obliquity angles, as well as the rotation period. To assess the uncertainties in the YORP effect's impact on the rotation, a randomized model was developed and employed to calculate how the YORP-induced drift standard deviations for various time frames relate to the YORP-induced drift rates and the uncertainties in the YORP effect's expression in terms of the spin orientation and rotation period. The model reveals that the YORP effect's uncertainties tend to converge to approximately 0.5 hours standard deviation at a time period of ten years for the majority of binary contact light curve analyzed asteroids. Moreover, the model reveals that the YORP-induced rotational period standard deviations for specific time periods, denoted as $\sigma_{\rm YORP}(T)$, can be determined by solving the following mathematical equation: $\sigma_{\rm YORP}(T) = \sqrt{\sum_{\rm all\ asteroids}\ P_{\rm all\ asteroids}\

The Facebook API update has limited the data accessible to researchers, significantly impacting large-scale analysis of user-generated content. This restriction hinders annual or longer temporal studies on social phenomena such as the spread of rumors, the evolution of subcultures, and election cycles. We contend that these events involve increased online activity and distinct patterns in how users interact with each other. We've collected and analyzed 10 million discussion threads from the "News" section of Facebook in the US during 2016, focusing on pre and post-Election Day periods. We've found that discussions about candidates show substantially higher levels of engagement from users compared to other topics, with users liking and commenting more frequently. These engagement patterns align with observed behaviors in the Twitter dataset. We've also found that users with more followers tend to have a like proportion that is consistent with those with fewer followers, which is similar to what is seen in the Twitter dataset.

This study makes the following contributions: It identifies specific homeomorphisms on a compact surface that, when fixed, prevent the overall group of homeomorphisms from being locally compact in a variant known as Roelcke uniformity. These homeomorphisms include those with a fixed point having a non-trivial local action, as well as those creating a non-trivial relationship between surface components when viewed in a local neighborhood. Furthermore, the study contributes to the sequence of prior results by showing that the subgroup of homeomorphisms that fix a singular point on the boundary of a disk is not Roelcke precompact.

Precise stellar characteristics are crucial for both astrophysics and exoplanetary science, particularly when studying M-dwarfs. Researchers have developed empirical relationships to determine these properties, yet inconsistencies in calibration standards lead to non-interchangeable results. To address this, our study establishes a new, unified framework for deriving stellar temperature, surface gravity, composition, as well as mass and radius from spectroscopic observations. This approach is validated using synthetic spectra and applied to real data, specifically the mass and radius of two newly discovered exoplanets from the K2 mission. The results show that adopting our unified stellar parameters leads to significantly different, more non-interchangeable exoplanet properties compared to previous analyses.

Confining modes at the edge, known as line waves, can propagate on the boundary between two specially designed electromagnetic interfaces that maintain mirror symmetry properties.
These line waves can occur in both electric and magnetic forms and are characterized by a high degree of mode confinement and stable propagation, unaffected by curvature and surface imperfections.
Due to their robustness, they hold significant potential for applications in secure communication, surface field access, and the development of new bending spacers.
To ensure effective and reliable performance, the design of line wave systems requires an understanding of how to compensate for curvature and to minimize the transmission of unwanted modes.
This study presents analytical and numerical approaches for developing dual-line wave systems, specifically focusing on bending line wave guides to create new applications.
The proposed approaches involve utilizing a point transformation to derive the governing equations and material properties required to maintain line wave behavior in curved and unrolled wave guides.
The experiments demonstrated in this study demonstrate the feasibility of these approaches, showing successful propagation and access of line waves in curved and unrolled wave guides.

Although a common practice, limiting query designs that incorporate self-joins is not universally applied in contemporary commercial databases. This study analyzes the impact of self-joins on the complexity of uniformly ordering the complete enumeration of query results, concurring with prior research that excludes self-joins. Building on existing algorithms for simpler queries, we develop efficient methods for enumerating complex queries with self-joins, including nearly output-optimal algorithms for certain complex cases. Additionally, we identify scenarios where self-joins cause an exponential increase in complexity, even for queries with straightforward structures and high-unionized components.

Multiple formal models can equivalently define functions that map infinite strings to other infinite strings, including MSO-transducers, streaming transducers, and certain two-way transducers. However, even when restricted to single passes through the input, some functions in these models can still be undecidable by Turing machines with infinite input, despite being defined by finite-state machines. To address this issue, a new decision-making approach is proposed for determining whether a specific function is computable and, if so, to create a Turing machine that accurately computes it.

Researchers have analyzed collision data with an integrated luminosity of 3 inverse femtobarns, and through amplitude analysis of specific two-body decay events, have discovered that the $B^0$ decay to a pair of $K^*$ mesons exhibits a higher fraction of longitudinal polarization than the $B^0_s$ decay to the same mesons. Furthermore, this difference in longitudinal polarization was utilized to determine the branching fraction of the $B^0$ decay to a pair of $K^*$ mesons.

A machine learning technique known as reservoir computing generates a model that mimics a complex system's behavior based on observed time-series data, and it has significant applications in understanding and designing coupled dynamical systems. Although highly effective for relatively simple systems, training data requirements increase significantly for more complex systems, and in conjunction with this, the accuracy of predictions offered by traditional reservoir computing techniques decline. We introduce a next-generation version of reservoir computing that overcomes these limitations, and it has the following benefits: it has the ability to function with a far smaller amount of training data, and it has the ability to offer more precise predictions. The advantages of this new version of the algorithm are demonstrated through modeling two systems with distinctly different levels of complexity, and the results show that it has the ability to function with up to ten times less training data, and it has the ability to surpass reservoir computing techniques currently used in the literature, and often with significantly larger amounts of training data.

A new bias-corrected estimator has been created for the mean absolute deviation of a median regression model, addressing the problem of irregularity that typically hinders conventional bias reduction.  To overcome this limitation, a specific alternative strategy was implemented.  Establishing the bias correction involves verifying the local asymptotic normality property and a specific Bahadur-Kiefer representation.  Developed within the context of a traditional asymptotic framework, this proposal appears to retain effectiveness in high-dimensional settings, as evidenced by simulation results.

To address scalability issues with Eulerian methods for finding optimal controllers under constraints and worst-case disturbances in variational Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs formulations, we've developed a second-order successive sweep algorithm for calculating the reachable state space. This approach, which assumes a continuous and smooth Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation, enables us to determine the states that are reachable within a given time frame by successfully integrating the characteristic system of first-order ordinary differential equations. Furthermore, we utilize Newton's method to efficiently find the time when characteristics intersect, thereby identifying the times and points where the solution's gradient discontinuities occur. Building on this foundation, we created an algorithm to visualize the characteristics' intersections using a reachability set generated by the First-Order Method (FOM). However, our team moved away from the FOM, choosing to implement a method that calculates the shortest first-order characteristics using Dijkstra's algorithm, which provides greater efficiency. As we anticipated, the results demonstrated a significant decrease in memory usage and computational time when using our algorithm compared to the FOM, yielding a more manageable reachability set with clear characteristic intersections. Moreover, we demonstrated our method's ability to solve a reach-avoid submarine pursuit-evasion problem with a higher-dimensional state space, achieving a substantial reduction in memory usage and computational time.

Multi-Layer Perceptrons are particularly effective at generating accurate
and complex signals for both images and videos. Using universal approximators
to directly model signals, especially high-resolution and real-time videos,
leads to significant improvements in performance and efficiency over traditional
methods that rely on functions composed of spatial representations. To achieve
this, we propose a cost-effective approach by decoupling the networks used to
approximate these signals, training them with a purpose-built, minimal
architecture. This method not only outperforms current autoenc-based solutions
at various evaluation metrics but also proves particularly effective when
applied to video compression, achieving remarkable results in terms of
performance and runtime, especially for videos with uniform content.

The underlying mechanisms of the ventral temporal cortex's animacy organization remain contentious, suggesting that animacy exists along a spectrum rather than a binary divide. Recent evidence suggests this continuum is influenced by the degree of presence or absence of distinct animal features or by how entities are perceived as social agents. In this study, a stimulus set with independent factors of visual categorizability and agency perception in animals was used to test these hypotheses through both computational neural networks and behavioral experiments. Utilizing functional magnetic resonance imaging, our findings showed that visual categorizability and agency perception separately explained independent components of the animacy spectrum in VTC. When combined, they fully captured the continuum, and our data indicated distinct posterior regions associated with each. The results of this study demonstrate the complex nature of the animacy spectrum in VTC, revealing multiple governing principles such as social agency that shape our understanding of this phenomenon.

The study proves the nonexistence of Landau-Siegel zeros or confirms quantum unique ergodicity for GL_2 Hecke-Maass newforms at a calculable pace, supported by the broader conclusion that Dirichlet L-function zeros exert a force pushing zeros from all other automorphic L-functions off the s=1 axis.

We have adapted the quantum relational Hoare logic originally proposed in (Unruh, POPL 2019) to incorporate "expectations" into preconditions and postconditions, thereby enabling the quantification of pre-/postconditions that reflect the relationship between programs' inputs and outputs when comparing pairs of programs.

The rapid transmission of contagious diseases is frequently amplified by a single high-transmission event, a super-spreader occurrence, which significantly boosts the epidemic's $R_0$ value and is often responsible for rapid spatial spread. Given that many epidemics exhibit rapid growth, the presence of a super-spreader seems inevitable. To understand this, we apply statistical principles from extreme value theory and branching processes. We show that, although unlikely, such events are necessary to explain the observed polynomial growth rates of epidemics, and they seldom happen during the disease's incubation period. Applying this concept to current data, we estimate the minimum number of super-spreaders needed in various geographic locations where the COVID-19 pandemic has been spreading.

Let's consider a complex topological vector space, denoted as X, along with the collection L(X) of continuous linear operators that act on X. This paper seeks to expand the concept of codiskcyclicity, initially developed for a solitary operator within L(X), to a broader context of operator sets defined as $\Gamma\subset L(X).$ Some key results regarding codiskcyclic collections of operators are proven, accompanied by a codiskcyclicity criterion. Furthermore, we demonstrate its practical utility by investigating the codiskcyclicity of C_0-semigroups comprised of operators.

The paper addresses the problem of bias in vector magnetic field maps, particularly in estimating the component perpendicular to the line-of-sight, Bperp. This issue has been identified in previous studies but a comprehensive analysis of its sources is novel. The study's findings are applicable to all magnetic field vector measurements, regardless of the method used. The analysis reveals that instrumental effects contribute minimally to the bias, with a few exceptions. Instead, the main contributors to the bias are non-uniformity in the instrumental response to magnetization levels, variations in solar activity during the observation periods, and the line-of-sight itself, which plays a significant role. To quantify the bias, the study introduces a general equation and uses specific examples to illustrate its components. The predicted bias values align with observed values, confirming the validity of the analysis. The study's conclusions are relevant to previous studies and has implications for future vector magnetic field instruments, particularly the ISHIMEI instrument scheduled for installation on the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope.

A comprehensive analysis has been conducted to measure the radii of 6097 young star clusters in 31 galaxies from the LEGUS survey. The custom analysis pipeline allowed for a large and contamination-resistant sample, enabling an in-depth investigation of the mass-radius relationship in star clusters. The results indicate a clear and broad relation between radius and mass, with a distinct peak in the relationship for clusters with masses between 10^4 M⊙ and 10^5 M⊙. The relationship can be represented by a bi-power law, with an associated slope that varies by galaxy type, with a steeper slope observed in early-type galaxies and a flatter slope in late-type galaxies. The effective radius of star clusters is also found to be related to the age of the cluster, with most of the radius-age relationship attributed to the movement of gases due to the cluster's own winds. The analysis confirms the prevalence of super-stellar associations and suggests that a significant portion of the observed radius distribution can be explained by these low-magnitude structures. The research has uncovered important insights into the formation and evolution of star clusters, with potential implications for our understanding of the radius-mass relationship and its variation across different galaxies.

We present a novel, direct method for calculating the decay width of hadrons
decaying to two photons, often requiring an indirect estimation via off-shell
form factors. The new method offers an uncomplicated way to study volume effects.
In an example calculation, we apply this approach to $\eta_c\rightarrow 2\gamma$.
Using lattice ensembles with three $N_f=2$ configurations at different lattice
spacings, we derive the final decay width $\Gamma_{\eta_c\gamma\gamma}=6.57(15)_{\textrm{stat}}(8)_{\textrm{syst}}$ keV,
considering systematics in the charm quark mass. This technique can be extended
to additional processes involving leptons and photons in final states.

A sign problem encountered in Monte Carlo simulations beyond half-filling can be mitigated by transforming the integration path. However, this transformation introduces an additional computational cost associated with the Jacobian determinant in the Boltzmann weight, posing a significant barrier for large-scale simulations. Our proposed architecture, based on a novel application of complex-valued affine coupling layers in neural networks, efficiently circumvents this challenge by achieving linear scaling of the determinant cost. As a result, this method allows us to tackle intractably large systems plagued by a severe sign problem.

This paper examines the relationship between integers that are y-friable (or y-smooth) and the Dickman function. By assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we derive a smooth version of the Dickman function, which allows us to obtain a specific subset of y-friable integers. This new function helps us to derive the density of the entire set of y-friable integers from the density of this specific subset. Additionally, without relying on unproven hypotheses, we can derive the connection between the Dickman function and the density of y-friable integers. This connection in turn enables us to estimate the prime-counting function $\pi(x)$ within the range $x \lt p \le 2x$.

Given any non-erasing free monoid morphism σ and subshift X, its image subshift Y under σ and the associated complexity functions p_X and p_Y exhibit the following relationship: there exist constants c, d, and C, where p_X scales by a factor of at least c times d, while scaling at most C, in the sufficiently large integers n in N. If σ is recognizable and letter-to-letter, then p_Y and p_X grow at similar rates, whereas if σ isn't letter-to-letter, there are instances where p_X isn't proportional to p_Y. As a result, topological entropy h_X isn't necessarily preserved when applying σ to X, indicating that defining topological entropy for free group currents F_N isn't feasible. Nevertheless, we can distinguish currents with or without zero or positive topological entropy.

By leveraging previously acquired skills and adapting them to unfamiliar tasks without explicit guidance, humans demonstrate impressive cross-task capabilities.
This study aims to enhance the cross-task generalization of language models by automatically identifying and leveraging latent skills within the model's architecture.
We introduce a novel framework that utilizes a skill discovery module, employing a contrastive learning approach to identify latent skills and a hierarchy-based optimization method to identify tasks related to each skill.
This approach enables each task to benefit from related skills, facilitating effective knowledge transfer.
Experimental results on the MultiToans dataset demonstrate that our proposed framework significantly outperforms baseline methods, showcasing the model's robust cross-task generalization.

This research introduces the m-arcsinh Kernel ('m-ar-K') Fast Independent Component Analysis ('FastICA') approach ('m-ar-K-FastICA') for feature extraction, combining kernel-based dimensionality reduction with ICA to overcome the limitations of previous methods. Although the kernel trick offers a powerful way to tackle non-linearity, its effectiveness can be undermined by a lack of open-source and reproducible kernel implementations, especially in complex datasets. The proposed m-ar-K-FastICA approach uses a readily available and adaptable Python library that facilitates collaboration with scikit-learn, providing a more reliable solution for feature extraction in the presence of random data. Experimental results using synthetic and real-world datasets show significant performance gains, especially in classification tasks, and highlight the approach's ability to outperform established methods like K-FastICA and show promising results when compared to deep learning approaches.

This work offers an overview of requirements engineering in the gaming sector.
Existing research studies on this topic have been comprehensively examined.
Key characteristics of the gaming industry were identified and their connections to broader market dynamics discussed.
In addition, several potential areas for further research within this field were briefly highlighted.

Optimizing hyperparameters in the private version of the stochastic gradient descent algorithm is a critical issue due to limited access to private datasets for hyperparameter tuning. The development of algorithms that efficiently find optimal hyperparameters for a favorable balance between privacy and performance within a predetermined search space is, therefore, crucial. In this paper, a generalized framework is established to address private hyperparameter optimization, and the framework is applied to demonstrate the effectiveness of popular methods, such as grid search, random search, and Bayesian optimization, within the context of differential privacy. The results of these algorithms are evaluated based on their computational costs, private convergence rates, and accuracy, and the most suitable algorithm is recommended for specific scenarios. The paper also provides a solution to optimize grid and random search methods by determining the ideal level of differential privacy necessary to achieve an optimal balance between privacy and performance.

For a Coxeter system denoted by (W,S), we develop the concept of a boolean complex consisting of involutions within W, mirroring Ragnarsson and Tenner's previous work. By applying discrete Morse theory, we identify the homotopy type of this boolean complex for a significant subset of Coxeter groups, including finite groups, revealing that its homotopy type is equivalent to that of a collection of spheres with dimension |S|-1. Moreover, we derive straightforward, recursive formulas to compute the number of spheres within this collection.

The Euclid satellite, set to launch in 2022, will significantly influence future cosmological research with its Visible and Near Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer instruments. The authors of this study analyzed how correlated readout noise affects in-flight measurements for the NISP detectors and proposed an analytical method for noise covariance matrices. Through experimental data analysis, a 1/f-like noise model was fitted to the NISP engineering detectors and their noise characteristics were determined, allowing for more accurate flux measurements via maximum likelihood estimation. It was found that using this approach, a four-fold decrease in measurement bias compared to the white noise model was possible. The authors conclude that even with the white noise model, negligible bias on NISP's in-flight measurements will be maintained, meeting Euclid's processing baseline requirements.

We applied an advanced statistical approach to examine the composition of 34,410 stars in the Milky Way disk using a vast dataset from the APOGEE-2. The study involved using a two-component model to break down elemental patterns into supernovae types and then comparing observed values to predicted values. The comparison yielded small discrepancies of up to 0.1 dex in some cases. The study revealed relationships between elements including a group sharing similar variations and distinct groups of elements with different behaviors. It also shed light on stars that the model struggled to accurately account for, likely indicating physical variations and small errors in measurements. The study enabled a controlled comparison of different star populations based on factors such as metal content. The findings revealed similar elemental patterns in outer regions of the galaxy, variations in satellite galaxies and star clusters like omega Centauri, and differences in abundance of elements in outer regions compared to inner regions. The study paves the way for a deeper understanding of the formation and chemical evolution of the galaxy.

The COVID-19 pandemic spread globally in early 2020 and caused severe consequences in China, also exacerbating public health anxiety fueled by rampant online rumors. To address this pressing issue, we examined the dynamics of rumor propagation and proposed a method to measure the impact of a rumor by tracking the speed of its new adopters. Utilizing search frequency as a proxy for this metric, we identified the peak and attenuation coefficients which conform to an exponential distribution. Subsequently, we developed and evaluated machine learning models to forecast these coefficients, finding that an attention distribution could effectively coefficient forecast the peak coefficient, whereas the attenuation coefficient was best predicted by an attention decay model. The effectiveness of these models in forecasting these coefficients exceeded existing methods, and interestingly, the coefficient forecast performance showed little variation compared to the historical data preceding major events. The coefficients associated with the 2020 H7N9 and Ebola epidemics further validate the generalizability of our proposed models.

A novel approach to measuring the distance to galaxies has been discovered by examining extragalactic planetary nebulae, specifically due to their nearly universal brightness pattern. Determining the precise distances to these galaxies, however, is complicated by the need to account for various factors including the nebula's structural diversity, environmental influences, and velocity-related effects. Leveraging advanced computational modeling and observational evidence, researchers developed an advanced tool known as LEVIATHAN to automate this process. By utilizing a comprehensive spectral database generated from numerous planetary nebulae across multiple galaxies, LEVIATHAN is capable of extracting accurate luminosities and velocities from a broad range of observations. When applied to the newly discovered Hubble Space Telescope inventory of the Milky Way's companion galaxy, M31, this tool enabled the calculation of the nebula's distance and velocity, along with a detailed exploration of its structural characteristics.

To effectively work with physiological data, it necessitates integrating and analyzing large amounts of data from multiple sources in real-time, which can be achieved with custom programs or advanced data processing engines. To these users' benefit, they should have access to high-level, efficient, and intuitive tools for handling and querying this data. We've developed a Python-based Python stream processing engine called LifeStream, which is specifically designed for physiological data and incorporates features like a intuitive query language, real-time visualization, and automatic data normalization. By leveraging LifeStream, researchers have demonstrated its capability to handle significant volumes of data and process complex, real-world physiological datasets in a single pass.

This research paper confirms that certain types of curves, specifically those in higher dimensional space, do not fit the classification of Bertrand curves except in two-dimensional Euclidean space. A new category, called the timelike (1,3)-Bertrand curve, is defined and characterized for the wider spatial context. The study provides necessary and sufficient conditions for a curve to fit this classification, and examples are also presented to illustrate the findings.

The choice of loss function for a neural network is widely regarded as a key decision with far-reaching implications, given the numerous loss functions developed to date, making it crucial to carefully select one. Despite its significance, research on the topic often omits explicit justification for loss function selection. We contend that this lack of justification reflects an untested assumption prevalent within the deep learning community. In this research, we investigate how loss function impacts performance in a supervised classification context. Our findings reveal that certain, previously underappreciated loss functions, including the KL divergence, can yield superior outcomes compared to established methods, underscoring the need to view loss function choice as a parameter amenable to optimization, rather than a fixed constant.
A stabilizable boundary feedback controller is designed for the Navier-Stokes equations using a linear control scheme with an oblique boundary orientation.

This research aims to advance the understanding of thermomechanical behavior in polymer crystallization. Strain-induced crystallization plays a significant role in polymer mechanical and thermal properties and must be accounted for during production and final product application design. To effectively capture its mechanical and thermal impacts, the proposed model utilizes a unique decomposition approach to the deformation gradient and applies the Coleman--Noll procedure and minimum dissipation potential principle to material modeling. The resulting model includes suitable Helmholtz free energy and dissipation potential assumptions, which enables simulation of crystalline region formation, degradation, and temperature changes during cyclic loading tests. Numerical implementation based on the finite element method provides the basis for numerical solutions, which include simulations of material sample microstructure and temperature evolution.

To analyze the impact of external magnetization on doped Bi$_2$Se$_3$ with spin-triplet nematic superconductivity, we computationally investigate magnetic susceptibility in nematic and chiral superconducting states using the Ginzburg-Landau formalism near its critical temperature. A key observation in this analysis is that the superconducting order parameter shows a retreating response to the applied field along the surface and a contrasting, expanding reaction along the bulk, which is indicative of the Larkin-Ovchinnikov effect. Moreover, the magnetic susceptibility is found to be significantly influenced by the shape of the Fermi surface, particularly the size of the electron pockets within the Bi$_2$Se$_2$Se layer, as well as the characteristics of the parent compound, including the strong SOC in the valence band and the weak SOC in the conduction band. A novel, unusual phenomenon is that the LO limit occurs along the c-axis in Bi$_2$Se$_2$Se with a hexagonal crystal structure, in contrast to other systems where it typically arises in the perpendicular direction to the Fermi surface. Finally, the magnetic field's effect on the superconducting critical state is analyzed.

One significant issue in Imitation Learning (IL) is that obtaining perfect optimal demonstrations from a teacher is a challenging task due to the complexities involved, especially in robotics. This issue arises because the process of collecting data requires a robot to execute complex tasks until successful completion, resulting in an expensive and time-consuming quality assurance process. Such high costs for data collection and feedback are unavoidable as the environment becomes more unstructured. To overcome this limitation, a positive feedback loop is essential, allowing for the use of multiple teacher policies simultaneously. Thus, even costly quality assurance processes can be justified, resulting in more optimized feedback for each piece of data collected. This is especially relevant in the context of autonomous vehicles where the quality of teacher demonstrations is often compromised. To address this challenge, a new protocol is introduced that allows for the use of multiple teacher policies simultaneously with a single feedback signal. This protocol leverages the advantage of reward shaping, allowing for multiple demonstrations to be combined simultaneously. As a result, a new method called Multi-Teacher Imitation Learning with Positive Feedback (MTI-LPF) is introduced. This method allows for the use of feedback from multiple teachers simultaneously, even costly quality assurance processes are involved.

Continuous phase modulation detection using conventional differential detection techniques is highly resistant to various channel disturbances, such as phase and Doppler shift. Its basic structure makes its implementation uncomplicated, involving the product of a received baseband signal and a time-reversed version of one symbol duration. Nevertheless, it experiences reduced signal-to-noise ratio compared to coherent detection methods. In this research, the performance of conventional differential detection is enhanced through increased delay periods. By accounting for $K$ symbol delays, the trellis structure and relevant branch and cumulative metrics are derived, resulting in an optimized criterion for $K$. This criterion is based on the minimum Euclidean distance between differential signals, ultimately facilitating the selection of ideal delay periods for popular CPM formats through simulated error rates verification.

New findings from 1D core-collapse simulations differ significantly from standard parametric models, especially in how collapsed stellar cores behave just before they collapse, with notable variations in their hydrostatic equilibrium states. This research utilizes these detailed 1D core-collapse simulations within 3D star formation simulations to investigate their impact on the predicted detection rate of merging black-hole and neutron-star systems, pertain to gravitational waves, in contrast to black-hole and neutron-star systems. By incorporating a more detailed prescription, we predict an increase of 40 percent in the detection density of merging black-hole and neutron-star systems, with the largest 600 percent increase in high-density regions of stellar clusters.

A previously reported finding from the research of the 1990s and 2000s is the strikingly uniform value of the ratio of variations to the mean in the energy density of quantum fields across various spacetime settings. Initially calculated using correlators of quantum field stress-energy tensors, the issue will now be re-examined using quantum thermodynamics. This is accomplished by determining the thermodynamic quantities known as heat capacity and quantum compressibility in model quantum fields in their thermal equilibrium states, specifically in $k$-vacuum states within $t+k$-space and in chiral quantum fields on Minkowski space. It is demonstrated that the ratio of quantum fluctuations to the mean in these settings is directly linked to the product of these quantities, which is found to match the outcomes obtained from field correlators. Additionally, explicit formulae are provided for free bosonic and fermionic fields in $t+k$-space.

Current deep learning techniques for removing rain from images have achieved notable success in processing artificially created rainy images.  Nonetheless, they struggle when confronted with more complex and realistic rain patterns, and as a result, are often incapable of effectively removing rain from truly rainy images, and in some cases, produce outputs that fall short of being fully clear and clean.  Existing solutions, as a rule, rely on a straightforward linear mapping between rain transmission and image brightness, and due to the inherent non-linear nature of this relationship, tend to result in inaccurate estimations of clear images, and in some cases, lead to outputs that are plagued with rain patterns and lack detail.  To address these limitations, we propose a novel non-linear rain transmission model, and leverage its properties to incorporate elaborate rain pattern generation, and as a consequence, establish a enhanced training framework that is aimed at producing clear, high-detail images with enhanced rain pattern simulation.  Our approach, and as a result, demonstrates exceptional disentanglement of rain and background, and lead to significant surpassing of existing methods on both synthetic and truly rainy images, and in some cases, result in outputs that are fully clear, detailed and free of rain patterns.  Our approach, and as a result, sets a new benchmark for state-of-the-art performance on the extensive outdoor scenes of the SDWRA dataset, and lead to exceptional visual quality and detailed preservation, and in some cases, result in exceptional clarity and detail.  Our approach, and as a

A prominent paradigm in reward learning utilizes human feedback via comparative evaluations, but their broader adoption is hindered by the expense and labor intensity of these comparisons. To overcome this limitation, we propose grouping multiple comparisons together and allowing human labelers to mark sub-regions of a condensed state space representation, thereby efficiently leveraging human time. Through data visualization techniques, we create an interactive interface for users to label these regions, thereby effectively enhancing the learning agents' performance, even when human labeling time remains constant, across basic Mujoco tasks.

We discuss recent research findings regarding model companions in set theory within the context of ongoing debates in the philosophy of mathematics. Initially, we explore how the concept of model companions is affected by the signature, before specifically examining the dependence of model companions in set theory. Our analysis indicates that the most intrinsic model companions for set theory correspond to $KD_5$, the fifth-order expressible fragment of ZFC. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Continuum problem does not affect model companions in $KD_5$ or first-order logic. It's also worth noting that various commonly studied extensions of ZFC, such as V=L, $\exists\in$-collection, and the axiom of constructibility, have the same model companions as ZFC itself.
This study establishes conditions and proof of existence for a modified Branson-Paneitz equation under Navier boundary conditions on a finite region of n-dimensional Euclidean space.

Evaluating a person's risk of drug abuse is crucial, and online surveys have proven effective for gathering relevant data. The data collection process included a comprehensive assessment of the participants' personality traits using the Big Five model, along with demographics and other key indicators. The data set, which includes responses from nearly 4000 volunteers, is made available to researchers to facilitate further analysis and modeling of this complex and multifaceted problem. The researchers demonstrated several simple models that can effectively predict a person's likelihood of drug abuse with an accuracy of around 75 percent.

Our proposed dataset, ATOMIC, is an exhaustive collection of everyday commonsense reasoning rules comprising nearly a million text-based descriptions.  This atlas of inferential knowledge, structured as conditional relationships (if X, then Y), stands out from other available datasets that are centered on categorization, by providing a framework that accounts for causality and effects, actions versus thoughts, and intentional versus unintentional actions.  We have developed nine categories of these relationships and demonstrated the efficacy of incorporating these patterns into models of artificial intelligence.  Our findings reveal that through generative training on ATOMIC, our models have gained a capacity for basic reasoning about events that are novel.  This is supported by test results showing that machine learning models incorporating these patterns achieve more accurate outcomes in relation to models operating in isolation as judged by both automated assessments and human feedback.

Portfolio optimization is a critical application in Finance, yet its computational complexity increases significantly with the number of assets, making it computationally challenging. Portfolio selection is typically formulated as a constrained quadratic minimization problem, which, when including future returns predictions, becomes an inequality-constrained system of linear equations. As expected, the computational difficulty escalates accordingly.

In 2019, Farhi and Lloyd introduced the first fully-quantum portfolio optimization methodology, leveraging the HHL quantum algorithm for its solution. Their approach was, however, based on the assumption of known probability distributions, which is uncommon in Financial applications. This study explores the hybrid-quantum portfolio optimization technique, incorporating the Monte Carlo simulation method for generating sample asset returns. We compare this approach to the original Farhi-Lloyd methodology and present the results of executing the algorithm using both synthetic and real-world financial data sets.

To enhance data efficiency of state-of-the-art end-to-end ASR models and enable them to handle a large amount of unpaired text data through multi-modal training, it's essential to address two challenges: synchronizing the sampling rates of speech and language features and ensuring that the learned representations from both encoders are consistent. This paper introduces a novel bidirectional attention mechanism that combines the learning of both the ASR and text encoders using a multi-modal learning method. This attention mechanism facilitates the exchange of sampling rates, effectively allowing the quality of transformed features to be measured in an alternative space. This leads to speech representations being enriched with more linguistic information, while the text representations are made more similar to speech, enabling ASR models to effectively leverage unpaired text data for pretraining. Experimental evaluations on the Librispeech corpus reveal a significant 6.15% reduction in word error rate when only paired data is used and up to 9.23% when additional unpaired text data is applied.

This analysis addresses the challenge of optimizing cross-sectional area through a specific point within a geometric form. To generalize this concept, the approach is expanded across multiple dimensions. It's shown that, for two-dimensional shapes, the average cross-sectional width is equivalent to the average chord length obtained by randomly selecting a direction and then selecting a distance from the origin following a uniform distribution. The relationship between this average measure and the perimeter of convex shapes is examined, demonstrating that the average cross-sectional length of convex shapes is at most equal to three-fourths of the perimeter. The approach is extended to two-dimensional shapes, where the distribution is changed to the inverse of the area of the resulting cut pieces. A comparable inequality is derived for this case as well. Finally, the work is further generalized to higher-dimensional spaces.

This paper investigates the long-term behavior of a randomly generated uniform parking distribution of size $n$, denoted as $\pi_n$. We establish that the first $k_n$ positions of $\pi_n$, $\pi_n(1)$ through $\pi_n(k_n)$, are asymptotically independent and identically distributed with a uniform probability distribution over the set $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ for two different distance metrics. When the number of initial positions $k_n$ grows at a rate slower than $\sqrt{n}$ for the total variation distance and slower than $n$ for the Kolmogorov distance, this asymptotic behavior is shown, thereby extending previous findings by Diaconis and Hicks. Furthermore, this work also derives rate bounds and statistical limit theorems for the sum or the maximum of the first $k_n$ parking locations. Our main approach to achieving these results is by utilizing conditioned random walk reformulations.

Measurements of superconducting nanowires, particularly NbN nanowires, indicate the presence of a critical voltage threshold for dc conduction below which coherent quantum phase slips dominate, potentially blocking conduction. The critical voltage of these nanowires is observed to be tunable using an adjacent gate electrode and varies significantly in response to applied voltage, aligning with expected results of quantum interference. The pattern of the critical voltage as a function of magnetic field matches numerical predictions, confirming that both quantum interference and external influences are pivotal factors.

The discovery of T-dwarf GJ 229B in 1995 offered initial insight into its composition, yet a detailed analysis with current spectroscopic methods has been lacking, especially concerning its atmospheric features, which display significant variability and faintness. By applying the open-source spectral synthesis tool gluesse to this object's full available spectrum, our study obtained the most accurate estimates for GJ 229 B's mass, which we found to be (357$\pm$9.) $M_{\rm Jup}$ with minimal bias due to distance estimates, and its temperature, which we located at (1317, 1366)$\rm \ K\ $ at the 68th percentile, independent of distance estimates. Although our analysis confirmed the object's primary nature, it revealed discrepancies in previously reported values for its distance, surface gravity, and age, especially in instances where the distance and mass were derived in a circular manner. Although our results do not uncover any substantial bias in the estimated ages of host stars, they offer a fresh perspective on determining ages, which often rely on assumptions about the system's evolution, rather than on the host star's cooling, as suggested by Fuhrman et al. (2021) with a 6.24\ Gyr age for the host star and a 6.5\ Gyr age for the system. Additionally, our study found that mass and age

Our study offers an explanation of the structural properties of a thermal medium,
primarily focusing on the interplay between parton distribution and structure functions.
Our approach incorporates finite parton virtuality and incorporates the effects of color
and flavor numbers. Through the use of the leading twist, leading power approximation,
we derive an approximate factorization of structure functions into distribution functions.
This factorization is facilitated by an impact factor formalism that accounts for the
dynamics of a virtual parton interacting with the thermal medium. As a result, we can
obtain the leading order structure functions from this method. However, a strict adherence
to the leading twist, leading power approximation requires the parton's energy to exceed
its mass in the forward direction. This also leads to a specific structure for the
corresponding impact factors. Consequently, the approximation of Bjorken scaling
is restricted to this regime. Additionally, we identify a regime of Bjorken scaling
that occurs at high energies and results in the radiated particle having a lower
average energy compared to the incident particle.

Our proposed approach tackles the challenge of novel view video prediction, taking input from multiple viewpoints. Unlike existing research that relies on narrow angle variations, our network can generate videos from significantly wider angles, up to 45 degrees, without the need for prior knowledge. By processing only RGB frames, we've developed a two-component representation, combining local and global features that enables novel view prediction. Our model achieves remarkable results on real-world datasets NTU-RGB+D and CMU Panoptic, surpassing the state-of-the-art in novel view video prediction, demonstrating significant gains in SSIM, PSNR, and FVD scores of 26.1%, 13.6%, and 60% respectively, without the use of prior views.

In this research, inter-orbital coupling was demonstrated using femtosecond laser writing, which enables orthogonal modes in a photonic lattice to couple with each other at different spatial locations. We characterized an asymmetric double-well structure, mapped its propagation dynamics and successfully created a device capable of spatial mode conversion anywhere within a photonic chip. Utilizing higher-order photonic mode phase structure, our experiment showed that a trimer configuration can serve as a $\pi$-phase beam splitter for multiplexing and other interference-based photonic applications.

The Ω-baryon, which contains sss quarks and was discovered at Fermilab in 1979, has a complex internal structure that is not fully understood. To gain deeper insights, it is essential to examine its properties using both experimental and theoretical approaches. Despite many Lattice calculations of the Ω-baryon's mass, there has been a discrepancy with the experimental value for over thirty years. However, recent advances, including Lattice results from the BMW collaboration in 2018, have significantly reduced the error bar below 1%, allowing for a more accurate comparison with the experimental value. This study involves comparing the absolute and relative electromagnetic charges, magnetic moments, and tensor moments of the Ω-baryon, utilizing the Light Front Holographic model and available Lattice data.

Airborne transmission risk in confined environments like buses is intricately affected by the interplay between turbulent airflow, respiration processes, coughing, and sneezing, as well as various ventilation methods, temperature-driven buoyancy effects, and surface deposition of aerosols. A computational model was employed to analyze the virus-laden aerosol transport on a typical London route, revealing a distinct flow pattern that results in the accumulation of aerosols near the floor by the end of the trip. Implementing a single fan for ventilation proved ineffective, as it primarily impacted air currents near the fan, leaving the rest of the bus largely unaffected. In contrast, a central air handling unit was able to limit the virus-laden aerosol concentration near susceptible individuals to below 10% of that affecting the same people under natural confluence.

Building on cutting-edge experimental projects such as HIBEF at the XFEL, our calculations investigate the birefringent scattering of x-rays when interacting with two combined optical lasers, considering various possible outcomes. To aid in detecting quantum vacuum effects experimentally, our analysis focuses particularly on situations where x-ray photons show differences not just in polarization, but also in direction of propagation and potential energy changes.

This note outlines the algorithm devised by J. M. Eisenlohr and S. L. Farris to
systematically generate all fully transitive polyhedra in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Furthermore, this algorithm is employed to construct a novel polyhedron within three-dimensional Euclidean space.

Broadbent and Lord introduced the concept of unclonable encryption, a unique feature in an encryption scheme where an adversary can't produce two encrypted versions of the same original message. This research extends this concept to related-key attack scenarios, an approach commonly used to identify vulnerabilities in public-key schemes. Specifically, we've investigated two types of related-key unclonable encryption conceptions: $\\mathsf{KRUC}$ and $\\mathsf{KRRC}$. Both conceptions involve adversaries with access to pairs of correlated ciphertexts, generated from the same original message but with one key derived from the other through a randomized function. Notably, we've found that even related-key encryption schemes based on learning parities with an error, or public-key encryption, including fully homomorphic encryption, are incapable of achieving related-key unclonability.

This study confirms that physical layer-based authentication is achievable in
Gaussian noise environments, with the caveat that an all-knowing adversary cannot
be overcome. An scenario is defined where an adversary with knowledge of the
channel's statistics seeks to impersonate the legitimate user to a recipient with
similar awareness. A successful impersonation occurs when the adversary can
transmit a message indistinguishable from the legitimate user's transmission.
It is demonstrated that the secure authentication region can be defined within this
framework and found to be non-zero even with the adversary having unlimited
channel access. Notably, in this model, secure authentication becomes feasible as
long as the adversary's transmission power is limited to less than the legitimate
user's transmission power.

We utilized the full tight-binding model and random phase approximation to
explore flat-band plasmons in hole-doped twisted bilayer molybdenum disulfide.
Our calculations showed that lattice vibrations can significantly dampen flat-band
plasmons, but under high hole-doping rates or appropriate optical phonon
considerations, distinct low-damped or quasi-flat plasmon modes emerge.

This paper expresses the potential function $f$ associated with an almost conformal gradient Ricci soliton on a Sasakian manifold in terms of the scalar field $p$, determining when the manifold is conformally equivalent to a Ricci flat manifold, and establishes a lower bound for $f$ in terms of $\lambda$, $\lambda_1$, and $\lambda_2$, where $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ represent the minimum and maximum eigenvalues of the tensor $S$.

Both celestial bodies can experience mass loss due to an expansive outward flow,
often regulated or redirected by magnetic fields that create a surrounding
magnetospheric field. Powerful star winds are generated by the scattering of the
star's radiative force, whereas in smaller stars and our Sun, weaker mass loss is
caused by thermal expansion of the mechanically heated outer layer. This process
can also occur in planets around low-mass stars, resulting in thermal expansion or
mechanical wear on their atmospheres. Magnetospheres in stars arise from wind flow
containment, whereas planetary magnetospheres are shaped by the external impact of
the star's wind. However, in both cases, magnetic reconnection due to the strain can
lead to detectable phenomena like X-ray flares and radio bursts. This review aims to
summarize the underlying physics of these processes and their shared and unique
aspects in stars and planets.

The Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect involves a rise in Spin-Orbit Coupling near a strong spin-orbit material's interface with an adjacent layer. This phenomenon has been observed in various systems, such as graphene and ferromagnetic layers, and controlling Spin-Orbit Coupling may lead to the discovery of novel phases in superconductor and semimetallic systems. In the study presented here, magnetoelectrical transport, specifically magnetoresistance and the anomalous Hall effect, were investigated in Cobalt/Bismuth multilayers in search of Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect. Measurements of the anomalous Hall effect and the layer-dependent Bismuth thickness revealed that this effect arises from Bismith's intrinsic property rather than its Berry Curvature, as the anomaous Hall ratio was found to be the Bismuth thickness-dependent. To reduce the contribution of the Bismuth's intrinsic magnetoelectrical transport, a Bismuth monolayer was isolated from the Cobalt by an extremely thin Oxide layer, and under these conditions, the anomalous Hall ratio decreased from 89 Ohm^{-1} m^{-1} to 29 Ohm^{-1} m^{-1}. Measuring the Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect required a negative Hall angle, and it was found to be present in samples with 1 monolayer Bismuth and 2-4 nanometers of the adjacent Bismuth layer.

This paper provides approximate solutions to the fractional time-independent Schrödinger equation in $N$-dimensional space for a generalised Mie-type potential, expressed as $V(r^{\alpha})=A/r^{2\alpha} + B/r^{\alpha} + C$, with the fractional parameter $\alpha$ affecting the space variable $r$. As $\alpha$ equals 1, the potential becomes the original Mie-type potential, commonly studied in physics. Using the Jumarie type fractional derivative approach, solutions are obtained and expressed in terms of the Mittag-Leffler function and a fractionally defined confluent hypergeometric function. Verification of results is achieved by comparison with existing works, particularly for $\alpha=1$. Numerical examples, including a diatomic molecule, demonstrate energy eigenvalue and bound state eigenfunction calculations.

We analyze how enforcing a neural network's Lipschitz continuity, as it pertains to input sensitivity, affects its performance. In order to investigate this, we developed a straightforward approach to determine the upper bound for a neural network's Lipschitz constant, taking into consideration various $p$-norms commonly used. This approach enables us to frame training a neural network with a limited Lipschitz constant as an optimisation problem that can be resolved via constrained stochastic gradient descent. Through our experiments, we found that models trained using this approach consistently performed better than those using alternative methods of regularisation. We further found that selecting hyperparameters is relatively straightforward and demonstrated the relationship between chosen norms and the resulting model's performance. The benefits of our approach are especially apparent when neural networks are trained on limited datasets.

Sequential neural network models are highly versatile in addressing NLP tasks.
Their sequential design leads to fundamental questions regarding their capacity
to learn complex language hierarchies and grammatical patterns naturally
occurring in human language.
As a case study for understanding the implicit comprehension of sentence
structure and the adoption of a hierarchical approach to parsing, we explore
two languages with distinct morphosyntential properties - English and Basque.
Our study focuses on the challenge these languages pose in predicting agreement
patterns.
We analyze the learning difficulties sequential models face and examine their
resulting representations of sentence structure and potential biases.
Our analysis leverages multiple data sources, including actual human performance
on a comprehension test related to the GEC corpus, as well as various metrics
assessing the quality of the models' underlying representations.
Our results indicate that sequential models struggle to grasp the hierarchical
aspects of sentence structure in both English and Basque - they tend to rely
on local cues and are prone to similar representational limitations and biases
across the two languages.
To mitigate this, we introduce a novel approach to architecture modification -
a cross-attention module that enables us to emulate different approaches to
handling dependencies within the grammar.
This allows for a comparative analysis of the original RNN architecture and the
proposed variant, highlighting the limitations of both in modeling the
aspects of sentence structure and agreement in English and Basque.

The discovery of HD 8655b, a rare super-Jupiter in a highly eccentric orbit around a distant star, offers an exciting opportunity to study how planetary movement affects the evaporation of atmospheres and the formation of scars on the planet's surface due to heat differences.  Although the planet's unique orbit causes a significant variation in the heat it receives from the star, the scarring it experiences from this heat fluctuation is more pronounced than the heat's effects, which could make HD 8655b an ideal candidate for finding these thermal patterns.  By observing the temperature patterns of the planet's atmosphere, which can be done using direct imaging, we may be able to find these thermal patterns and understand the evolution of the planet's atmosphere.  However, this is a challenging task, which could be made easier if the planet's position relative to its star is known, which in turn allows for the direct measurement of the planet's atmospheric evolution.  If direct imaging is not possible, the formation of the planet's atmosphere may be understood by observing the changes in the planet's composition as it moves along its eccentric orbit, provided that the planet's position relative to its star is known, which in turn allows for the measurement of the planet's atmospheric evolution. Customized digital games successfully encourage motivation in repetitive exercises required for motor rehabilitation; however, currently there is no universal approach to creating them, and the influence of adding competition elements on players' drive to complete necessary repetitions is unclear. To design a general framework for developing customized games, we analyze existing methods and propose a purpose-driven approach. We also experiment with adding competition to a basic customized game and observe an increase in motivation to complete necessary repetitions, as well as a rise in overall engagement and focus among participants when competition is incorporated.

Our research offers a variational approximation, drawing from the Ambrosio-Tortorelli model, to quantify brittle fracture energies in complex, piecewise-rigid structures, applicable to both nonlinear and linearised elasticity frameworks.

We investigate the possibility of lepton-flavour non-universality in certain processes at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). To this end, we focus on Drell-Yan ditau production and calculate precise corrections to this process, taking into account the effects of quantum chromodynamics at the next-to-leading order. A specialized code is developed to efficiently generate these corrections, allowing for more accurate simulations of ditau events. By applying these simulations to recent LHC data, we can place constraints on a type of exotic particle, known as vector leptoquarks, based on their mass and coupling strength. This code is an important tool for ongoing and future searches for such particles at the LHC, as future iterations will be employed in official analysis of data from these collisions.

Radiation exposure during positron emission tomography (PET) scans restricts their usage for sensitive groups, such as pregnant women and young individuals requiring frequent imaging, due to compromised image quality from lower doses or shortened scan times. Deep-learning models have made significant advancements in enhancing PET images by learning mappings from corresponding low-quality and high-quality PET images, but they have primarily focused on using large datasets with high statistical significance (Osborne et al. 2020). We address this limitation by aiming to evaluate the effectiveness of popular PET image denoising networks under significantly reduced statistical conditions, such as those with low dose acquisitions and shorter scan times. To achieve this, we conducted a comprehensive assessment of popular PET image denoising models by adapting state-of-the-art deep learning frameworks, checking their performance against widely used baseline image acquisition enhancement techniques. We extensively tested these models across a broad data spectrum, learning mappings from corresponding low-noise and high-quality PET images, such as those obtained from standard 15-minute 68Ga-PET-CT scans, and also explored adaptations for significantly shorter scan times as little as 5 minutes, and even as low as 2 minutes. To further evaluate their performance under extremely low statistical conditions, we developed deep learning frameworks by adapting state-of-the-art models, checking their performance against widely used image acquisition enhancement baseline techniques. We conducted a comprehensive assessment of popular PET image denoising models by adapting state-of-the-art deep learning frameworks, checking their performance

The issue of tailoring news to individuals' interests while respecting their data remains unresolved. Growing worries about over-collected data and its unintended use have motivated our research on balancing personalization and privacy. Our experience creating personalized content platforms that protect users' confidentiality has sparked an investigation into users' attitudes towards these topics. A conducted survey revealed the opinions of various age groups regarding personalization and privacy. In this research, we are sharing our key discoveries with publishers and the community, and outlining potential paths for future studies.

A linguistic analysis known as centering theory (CT) explains how coherence in conversations emerges from the connections between successive statements. This paper explores the link between CT and advanced computer systems that identify relationships within a text. By developing specific metrics and a search-based method, the study examines if modern computer systems that recognize connections within a text align with the principles of CT. The analysis indicates a correlation between the systems' ability to recognize connections and their ability to model the coherence of the text, but also reveals that these computer systems are not fully capable of doing so. To address this shortcoming, the author proposes modifications to the existing system that would enhance their performance.

We have devised three new parameterized algorithms for identifying whether a directed graph can be represented in an upward planar layout. Specifically, we've developed a fixed-parameter algorithm based on the number of source vertices, an XP algorithm based on the graph's treewidth, and a fixed-parameter algorithm based on the treedepth parameter. Our novel method combines parameterized techniques with SPQR tree-decompositions, extending previous tractability findings on series-parallel graphs, single-source graphs, and outerplanar graphs.

The rising intricacy of modern adaptable systems demands elevated automation in their configuration process, thus also accelerating development cycles via rapid, automated workflow integration. A novel automated configuration framework is introduced, using model checking and SMT, adaptable to any domain definable by SMT formulas, allowing for modular scalability and improved human understanding via metric-driven optimization. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through its application to configuring a CGRA memory tile for diverse image processing tasks.

This study examines the operator growth phenomenon in Lie-symmetric systems by utilizing concepts from quantum information theory. We specifically analyze Krylov complexity, entanglement properties, and information capacity within Heisenberg spin systems that obey $su(2)$ symmetry. By leveraging the known structure of these operators in a Schwinger representation, we determine precise expressions for entropy and complexity in both ground states and time-evolved states. The findings reveal that growth rates in these spin systems align with those observed in more general $su(N)$ systems and can be explained through a link between operator growth and Lie symmetry itself.

Recently, WiFi has become the primary method for locating individuals or devices within indoor settings. This paper examines present techniques for positioning within indoor environments, with a focus on methodological issues related to data collection, data cleaning, and data analysis. A comprehensive discussion on the most common approach in the field, namely, WiFi fingerprinting, along with its sub-methods such as K-Nearest Neighbor, is included. This paper also outlines emerging directions and future directions in the area of indoor localization using WiFi. Specifically, a discussion on the application of machine learning to create more efficient localization systems with reduced data sets and improved accuracy is explored. A summary of current directions in the field of indoor localization using machine learning is discussed. This paper also discusses the use of machine learning to create more efficient localization systems with reduced data sets and higher accuracy, along with a summary of present techniques in the field of indoor localization using machine learning. A comprehensive overview of the most common approach in the field, WiFi fingerprinting, along with a discussion on the two main variants of this method, is included, along with other techniques for positioning within indoor environments, such as trilateration, triangulation, and angle of arrival. Moreover, a discussion on the main challenges and challenges associated with implementing machine learning to create more efficient localization systems, namely, large data sets, frequent data updates, storage costs, device compatibility, and security concerns, is included.
